summary: Frames per-task model routing for coding as a Context-Action-Feedback loop (a contextual bandit) and builds ACRouter: a fine-tuned Qwen3.5-0.8B orchestrator ensembled with heuristics, a verifier that scores outputs with AST parsing, sandbox runs, prompt-embedded tests and an LLM judge, and a kNN memory of past outcomes. It also releases CodeRouterBench (~10K tasks repurposed from 15+ benchmarks, scored for 8 frontier models). ACRouter has the lowest cumulative regret in-distribution and the best router score on a 176-task agentic OOD split.

claims.claim: The routing bottleneck is information deficit, not reasoning: adding per-dimension performance stats gives a +15.3% relative gain to an LLM router.
claims.evidence: Table 1 (Sonnet 4.6 router, 2,919 tasks): Vanilla 41.41 -> +Perf stats 47.74 AvgPerf%, vs DimensionBest 47.50 and Oracle 57.00; but Perf/$ falls from 1.97 to 1.71. Appendix C.1 repeats across all 8 router models (Table 7).

claims.claim: ACRouter attains the best in-distribution AvgPerf and lowest cumulative regret.
claims.evidence: §5.2/Table 3: 49.98% AvgPerf, CumReg 205.5 vs DimensionBest 47.50% (+2.48 pts) and bandits 297-307; cost $13.21 vs $12.89 DimensionBest and $34.02 Always-Opus (App. D.5). No seeds/CI for ACRouter; only the bandit baselines are 5-seed averaged.

claims.claim: ACRouter generalizes to OOD agentic programming, beating all routers and the strongest single model.
claims.evidence: Table 3 / App. D.7 Table 13: ACRouter 62.50% resolved on 176 tasks vs Always-Opus 57.14%, bandits 46-50%, static classifiers 8.93-21.43%. However §5.2 and D.7 also report a standalone GPT-5.4 backend resolving 75.00% of the same split — a single model beats the router by 12.5 pts, which the paper relegates to an appendix. 40-step limit instead of 250 (Limitations).

claims.claim: No single model dominates across coding dimensions.
claims.evidence: Fig. 4 / §4.2: Opus 4.6 highest average 42.9% but beaten by GLM-5 on algorithm design (47.2 vs 25.4) and Qwen3-Max on test generation (82.7 vs 39.2); 5 distinct dimension-best models. Three dimensions scored partly by LLM-as-judge with no validation reported.

patterns.note: Online, feedback-driven routing beats static routers and Always-Opus on cost-aware regret, but a single GPT-5.4 run beats the router on OOD agentic tasks (75.00% vs 62.50%).
kNN memory of verified past outcomes is the component credited with OOD gains over static classifiers.
Verifier uses sandbox execution and prompt-embedded tests (no ground-truth oracle) to produce feedback.
LLM-as-judge used for 3 of 10 dimensions and inside the Verifier; not validated against humans.
CodeRouterBench repurposes SWE-bench Verified and other public benchmarks; 'living benchmark'.
Reports token-priced cost; admits provider cache hits unobservable, so dollar cost is secondary.

methodology.sample: 10,111 tasks: 7,080 probing, 2,919 ID test, 176 OOD agentic (SWE-bench Verified, LongCLI-Bench, FeatureBench, SWE-CI).
methodology.baselines: Always-model, Random, DimensionBest, kNN, LogReg, TF-IDF+MLP, RouteLLM-MF/BERT, LoRA-finetuned Qwen3.5, LinUCB, LinTS — reasonably broad and current.
methodology.models: Pool: Claude Opus 4.6, Sonnet 4.6, GPT-5.4, Qwen3-Max, Qwen3.5-Plus, GLM-5, Kimi-K2.5, MiniMax-M2.7; orchestrator Qwen3.5-0.8B.
methodology.variance: Bandits 5-seed averaged; ACRouter and others single deterministic stream, no CI.
methodology.ablations: C-A-F component decomposition (§3.4); router-model sweep (App. C.1); Qwen scaling sweep (App. C.2).
methodology.contamination_controls: OOD tasks filtered for similarity to probing set; source benchmarks are public and likely in pretraining.
methodology.languages: Mixed per source benchmarks; OOD predominantly Python (SWE-bench-derived).

standards.peer_review: None; arXiv comment: '39 pages, 21 figures, a living technical report with a living benchmark that continuously updates'.
standards.artifacts: Code and benchmark at github.com/LanceZPF/agent-as-a-router; prompts in App. B.4.

biases.detail: Headline OOD win framed against Always-Opus while a stronger single-model result (GPT-5.4, 75.00%) is moved to an appendix.
Three of ten dimensions use proxy metrics plus LLM-as-judge without agreement checks.
ACRouter's +2.48-pt ID margin has no seeds or CI.
All tasks repurposed from public benchmarks (incl. SWE-bench Verified).
Authors' own benchmark, own regret metric, own system ranked first.
'Living' report/benchmark: numbers may change between versions, hindering citation.

coi.affiliations: National University of Singapore; DAMO Academy, Alibaba Group; Hupan Lab; Zhejiang University; UC Berkeley; HKUST.
coi.vendor_products_evaluated: Alibaba Qwen3-Max and Qwen3.5-Plus in the model pool; orchestrator is an Alibaba Qwen3.5-0.8B fine-tune.
coi.detail: Alibaba-affiliated authors use Qwen as router backbone and in the pool, but Qwen is not the headline winner (Opus/GPT-5.4 are strongest); vendor affiliation without clear self-promotion.

verdict_reason: Broad baseline set and released benchmark with a sensible regret framing, but small ID margins without variance, unvalidated LLM-judge dimensions, and the OOD headline is undercut by a single model (GPT-5.4) beating the router.
applicability: Per AGENTS.md, model choice belongs to the agent host or an opt-in BYOK gateway, not to `qr`. Read this paper as evidence about that host-side choice, not as a reason to put a router in the harness. For the Java team: the OOD result suggests that for multi-step agentic work across the several repositories, picking one strong model per host may beat a learned router; routing pays off mainly for cheap single-turn tasks such as test generation or small snippets. The useful harness-side idea is logging verified per-task outcomes (test pass, cost) in a shared, host-neutral store, so that any host's routing can be informed by evidence. No Java-specific evaluation.

conflicts_with.detail: Revelio finds that a static cheap-then-strong split (Haiku for scanning, Sonnet for confirmation) beats frontier single-model agents. Here a single frontier model (GPT-5.4) beats the learned router on agentic OOD tasks, so the value of routing depends on whether stages are decomposed.
